title: Model Spec
description:
A 3D asset described as data, on a game design's asset requirement (`asset_requirements[].model`). Not an artifact: a part of one.

Two uses. With `parts`, it is a BUILD SPEC: primitives, materials, clips, LOD ratios and a collision proxy that an offline tool builds headless into one GLB, deterministically, with no one opening an editor. Without `parts`, and always in addition, it is an EXPECTATION: every clip, LOD level, collision proxy, fitted size and budget it declares is checked against the delivered GLB, whichever source that came from — a purchased model with a renamed clip fails the same way a generated one would.

Coordinates are glTF's, which are the 3D runtime's: metres, +Y up, the model faces +Z. Rotations are Euler degrees, XYZ order. A budget written here is the design's own and an error when exceeded; the policy's defaults are warnings.

parts.description: The geometry, one glTF node per part, named by its id. Children follow their parent's transform and animation.

id.description: The node name at runtime: animation tracks and gameplay code find the part by it.

shape.description: A primitive fitted to `size`. Cylinders, cones and capsules stand along +Y; a plane lies in XZ facing +Y; a sphere is a UV sphere. A capsule's caps are hemispheres of the smaller of its x and z radii. `extrude`: the `outline` polygon (a top view) pulled up along +Y - a swept wing, a fin, a chevron, a blade, an arrow, any flat silhouette with thickness. `lathe`: the `profile` line swept round the Y axis - a nozzle, a bell, a dome, a bottle, a turned post. Both are fitted to `size` like the primitives.

outline.description: Extrude only: the polygon [[x, z], ...] in the part's XZ plane, seen from above (+X right, +Z the model's front), points in order around the shape, not crossing itself; concave is fine. Any unit: it is scaled so its bounding box is `size` x and z, and pulled up to `size` y. A mirrored part's outline is mirrored too.

profile.description: Lathe only: the line [[radius, y], ...] from one end to the other, swept round the Y axis in `segments` steps; radius >= 0, 0 only at the first or last point (closing that end to a point; an end with a radius gets a flat cap). Not crossing itself. Any unit: scaled so the widest radius is half of `size` x and z and the height is `size` y.

size.description: Bounding size in metres [x, y, z]. Zero only on a plane's y. Default [1, 1, 1].

position.description: Relative to the parent part, or to the model's origin. Default [0, 0, 0].

segments.description: Radial segments of round shapes. Default 16.

material.description: A material's id. None: the runtime's default material.

smooth.description: Smooth shading. Default true for spheres and capsules, false otherwise.

taper.description: [x, z]: the part's top (+Y) is scaled by these factors, linearly from 1 at its base - a torso wider at the shoulders, a cabin narrower at the roof, a tapered limb. `size` is the base's. Not on a plane.

bevel.description: Metres: the part's sharp edges (faces meeting at 30 degrees or more) are rounded off with two segments. Box, cylinder, cone and extrude only; at most a third of the part's smallest side.

mirror.description: Also build this part mirrored across the X = 0 plane of its parent (the model, for a top-level part): a second node `<id>-mirror`, its parent's mirror when the parent is mirrored too. Arms, legs, wheels and wings are written once.

materials.description: Metallic-roughness PBR, the only model the runtime renders without custom shaders. Reuse one material across parts: each is a draw call.

opacity.description: Below 1 the material blends: sorting cost at runtime.

texture.description: A generated base-colour texture, embedded in the GLB.

pivot.description: Where the model's origin ends up after building: the centre of its base (default, what placement on the ground wants), its centre, or where the parts put it.

fit.description: Scale the whole model uniformly so it measures `size` metres along `axis` (max: its longest side). Applied to the geometry, never left on a node.

animations.description: Named clips. Without tracks a clip is only an expectation: the delivered GLB must contain a clip of that name. Gameplay looks clips up by name, so the name is the contract.

loop.description: Advice to the runtime; glTF does not store it.

keys.description: Absolute values in the part's parent space, as the rest pose is written. Rotation in Euler degrees; keep each step under 180 degrees.

lods.description: Levels of detail beyond LOD0: a count (each halves the triangles) or decreasing triangle ratios. Not with animated parts. Only when the model is seen at several distances.

collision.description: A separate, unrendered collision proxy: never simulate against the visual mesh.

budget.description: Limits this design sets for this model. Exceeding one is an error.

fps.description: The rate clips are sampled at when built. Default 30.
